- `i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo` (1210) — vga_switcheroo path, also calls `i915_drm_suspend_late`

## 2. Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

**None — `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` does not exist in this tree.** The runtime-PM slot is:

```c
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,   /* i915_driver.c:1752 */
.runtime_resume  = intel_runtime_resume,
```

`intel_runtime_suspend` (i915_driver.c:1545-1642) is a **completely disjoint** call graph from `i915_pm_suspend`: it does *not* call `i915_drm_suspend`. It calls `i915_gem_runtime_suspend`, `intel_pxp_runtime_suspend`, `intel_gt_runtime_suspend` (per-GT loop), `intel_irq_suspend`, `intel_uncore_suspend`, `intel_display_power_suspend`, `vlv_suspend_complete`. So no `i915_pm_suspend` caller shares a callee with the runtime-suspend path except `intel_irq_suspend`.

## 3. `dev_priv` data flow: `i915_drm_suspend` → display suspend

`intel_display_suspend` doesn't exist either; the display suspend entry is `intel_display_driver_suspend`. `dev_priv` is **not** passed down — it is *narrowed* to `struct intel_display *`:

```
i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
  │  i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  ▼  &i915->drm                                     [struct drm_device *]
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)             i915_driver.c:1103
  │  dev_priv = to_i915(dev)                         [drm_i915_private *]  line 1105
  │  display  = dev_priv->display                    [intel_display *]     line 1106
  │
  ├─ disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm)   <- dev_priv field
  ├─ intel_power_domains_disable(display)                 <- narrowed
  ├─ intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display)
  ├─► intel_display_driver_suspend(display)  ── display only, dev_priv dropped here
  │       display->drm  -> drm_atomic_helper_suspend()
  │       display->restore.modeset_state = state     (writeback)
  │       flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup)
  │       intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)
  ├─ intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)                          <- dev_priv
  ├─ i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt)             <- dev_priv
  ├─ suspend_to_idle(dev_priv) -> opregion_target_state
  ├─ dev_priv->suspend_count++                            <- dev_priv mutated
  ├─ enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm)
  └─ i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv)
```

Key point: the `dev_priv → display` conversion at line 1106 is the boundary — everything below `intel_display_driver_suspend` sees only `struct intel_display *`, reaching back to the DRM device via `display->drm` rather than `dev_priv`.

Note: `i915_driver.c` is only partially indexed (unparsed lines incl. 1570, 1575, 1588, 1676, 1685), so graph-derived caller counts under-report; the above was verified against retrieved source.
